title.english: Referring to People: Pronouns, Names, Titles, and Family Terms

body:
## Japanese Rarely Says "You"

Textbooks introduce ⟦あなた→あなた：02565_anata⟧ early, but Japanese speakers seldom use it. To refer to the person they are talking to, they use the name with a suffix (⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧さん), a title (⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧, ⟦{部長|ぶちょう}→部長：01017_buchou⟧), or nothing at all, since the subject of a sentence is usually left out. ⟦あなた→あなた：02565_anata⟧ between people who know each other sounds distant, and to a superior it is rude; its most natural use today is a wife addressing her husband, or a form on which the reader is "you."

The other second-person words all carry a register:

- ⟦{君|きみ}→君：01384_kimi⟧ — to a junior or a close equal; mostly used by men, and by teachers to students.
- ⟦お{前|まえ}→お前：02533_omae⟧ — rough and masculine, between close male friends or downward; insulting to anyone else.
- ⟦あんた→あんた：27721_anta⟧ — casual and blunt, more common in western Japan and among older speakers.
- ⟦{貴様|きさま}→貴様：18458_kisama⟧, ⟦てめえ→てめえ：24800_temee⟧ — hostile, the words of a quarrel or a gangster film.

When in doubt, use the person's name with ⟦さん→さん：09848_san⟧, or no pronoun at all.

## Words for "I"

Japanese has several words for "I," and the choice tells the listener your gender, your age, and how formal you are being.

- ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧ — the neutral default for everyone in polite speech, and for women in casual speech too. Read ⟦わたくし→私：02987_watakushi⟧, the same kanji is the formal choice for speeches and business.
- ⟦{僕|ぼく}→僕：01729_boku⟧ — used by men and boys; soft and unassuming, acceptable in most settings short of the very formal.
- ⟦{俺|おれ}→俺：02185_ore⟧ — used by men among friends and family; rough and casual, and out of place with customers or superiors.
- ⟦あたし→あたし：28132_atashi⟧ — used by women in casual speech.
- ⟦うち→うち：27540_uchi⟧ — casual, mainly used by women and in the Kansai region.
- ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧ — "oneself"; some men use it as "I," which sounds disciplined, in the manner of sports teams and the military. In Kansai it can also mean "you."

The plurals follow the same pattern: ⟦{私|わたし}たち→私たち：28351_watashitachi⟧, ⟦{我々|われわれ}→我々：03795_wareware⟧ (formal, for a company or a group), ⟦{僕|ぼく}ら→僕ら：22784_bokura⟧. Most men switch between two or three of these words during the day, ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧ in a meeting and ⟦{俺|おれ}→俺：02185_ore⟧ with friends, and learners should do the same rather than pick one word for all occasions.

## Names, Suffixes, and Titles

A name is almost never used bare. It takes a suffix that marks the relationship:

- ⟦さん→さん：09848_san⟧ — the default for adults you are not close to, after the family name (⟦{山田|やまだ}→山田：09529_yamada⟧さん) or, among friends, the given name.
- ⟦{様|さま}→様：01549_sama⟧ — for customers, clients, and the addressee of a letter: ⟦お{客様|きゃくさま}→お客様：08780_okyakusama⟧, ⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧⟦{様|さま}→様：01549_sama⟧.
- ⟦{君|くん}→〜君：01998_kun⟧ — for boys and for men junior to you; teachers use it for students, and offices for junior staff.
- ⟦ちゃん→ちゃん：02003_chan⟧ — for small children, close friends, and family, with a warm and childlike feel: {美咲|みさき}ちゃん, ⟦お{兄|にい}ちゃん→お兄ちゃん：22785_oniichan⟧.
- ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧ — for teachers, doctors, lawyers, politicians, and writers, alone or after the name. Never use it for yourself.
- ⟦{先輩|せんぱい}→先輩：01451_senpai⟧ — someone senior to you in a school, club, or company, used as a form of address; ⟦{後輩|こうはい}→後輩：02501_kouhai⟧ names a junior but is not used to address one.
- ⟦{部長|ぶちょう}→部長：01017_buchou⟧, ⟦{課長|かちょう}→課長：01075_kachou⟧, ⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧, ⟦{店長|てんちょう}→店長：30461_tenchou⟧ — job titles double as names: ⟦{部長|ぶちょう}→部長：01017_buchou⟧、お⟦{電話|でんわ}→電話：01471_denwa⟧です (Boss, there's a call for you).

Using a name with no suffix at all is ⟦{呼|よ}び{捨|す}て→呼び捨て：15868_yobisute⟧. It is normal for family, close friends, and one's own subordinates, and offensive elsewhere. Two rules come from the inside/outside distinction that runs through Japanese: never put ⟦さん→さん：09848_san⟧ on your own name, and when you speak to outsiders about the people on your side, drop the honorifics — to a client, your boss Tanaka is ⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧, not ⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧さん or ⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧⟦{部長|ぶちょう}→部長：01017_buchou⟧.

## Family Terms: Inside and Outside

Family words come in two sets. One is plain and is used for your own family when you speak to outsiders; the other adds お or ご and ⟦さん→さん：09848_san⟧ and is used for other people's families. Inside the family, the honorific set is used to address older members, and younger members are called by name.

| Relation | Your own (to outsiders) | Someone else's | Addressing them at home |
|----------|------------------------|----------------|------------------------|
| father | ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧ | ⟦お{父|とう}さん→お父さん：02855_otousan⟧ | ⟦お{父|とう}さん→お父さん：02855_otousan⟧, ⟦パパ→パパ：01788_papa⟧ |
| mother | ⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧ | ⟦お{母|かあ}さん→お母さん：02851_okaasan⟧ | ⟦お{母|かあ}さん→お母さん：02851_okaasan⟧, ⟦ママ→ママ：03155_mama⟧ |
| older brother | ⟦{兄|あに}→兄：00570_ani⟧ | ⟦お{兄|にい}さん→お兄さん：02858_oniisan⟧ | ⟦お{兄|にい}ちゃん→お兄ちゃん：22785_oniichan⟧ |
| older sister | ⟦{姉|あね}→姉：00571_ane⟧ | ⟦お{姉|ねえ}さん→お姉さん：02859_oneesan⟧ | ⟦お{姉|ねえ}ちゃん→お姉ちゃん：27278_oneechan⟧ |
| younger brother | ⟦{弟|おとうと}→弟：00572_otouto⟧ | ⟦{弟|おとうと}さん→弟さん：27447_otoutosan⟧ | by name |
| younger sister | ⟦{妹|いもうと}→妹：00573_imouto⟧ | ⟦{妹|いもうと}さん→妹さん：27448_imoutosan⟧ | by name |
| grandfather | ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧ | ⟦おじいさん→おじいさん：02860_ojiisan⟧ | ⟦おじいちゃん→おじいちゃん：20642_ojiichan⟧ |
| grandmother | ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧ | ⟦おばあさん→おばあさん：02863_obaasan⟧ | ⟦おばあちゃん→おばあちゃん：10968_obaachan⟧ |
| husband | ⟦{夫|おっと}→夫：00982_otto⟧, ⟦{主人|しゅじん}→主人：00987_shujin⟧ | ⟦ご{主人|しゅじん}→ご主人：01593_goshujin⟧ | by name, ⟦あなた→あなた：02565_anata⟧, ⟦パパ→パパ：01788_papa⟧ |
| wife | ⟦{妻|つま}→妻：01005_tsuma⟧, ⟦{家内|かない}→家内：00958_kanai⟧ | ⟦{奥|おく}さん→奥さん：02853_okusan⟧ | by name, ⟦ママ→ママ：03155_mama⟧ |
| son | ⟦{息子|むすこ}→息子：00799_musuko⟧ | ⟦{息子|むすこ}さん→息子さん：30841_musukosan⟧ | by name |
| daughter | ⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧ | ⟦{娘|むすめ}さん→娘さん：30842_musumesan⟧, ⟦お{嬢|じょう}さん→お嬢さん：01566_ojousan⟧ | by name |
| parents | ⟦{両親|りょうしん}→両親：00806_ryoushin⟧ | ⟦ご{両親|りょうしん}→ご両親：30840_goryoushin⟧ | — |
| children | ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧ | ⟦お{子|こ}さん→お子さん：01564_okosan⟧ | — |

The viewpoint of the youngest child often rules at home: parents call each other ⟦お{父|とう}さん→お父さん：02855_otousan⟧ and ⟦お{母|かあ}さん→お母さん：02851_okaasan⟧, and grandparents are ⟦おじいちゃん→おじいちゃん：20642_ojiichan⟧ and ⟦おばあちゃん→おばあちゃん：10968_obaachan⟧ to everyone. ⟦{主人|しゅじん}→主人：00987_shujin⟧ (literally "master") and ⟦{家内|かない}→家内：00958_kanai⟧ ("inside the house") are the traditional words for one's spouse; many younger speakers now prefer ⟦{夫|おっと}→夫：00982_otto⟧ and ⟦{妻|つま}→妻：01005_tsuma⟧.

## He, She, and "That Person"

⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧ and ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧ mean "he" and "she," but they also mean "boyfriend" and "girlfriend," and they are not used for superiors. In practice, third persons are named the same way as second persons — ⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧さん, ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧, ⟦{部長|ぶちょう}→部長：01017_buchou⟧ — or pointed to:

- ⟦あの{人|ひと}→あの人：25922_anohito⟧ — that person; ⟦あの{方|かた}→あの方：16618_anokata⟧ is the polite version.
- ⟦こちら→こちら：00960_kochira⟧ — this person, when introducing someone: ⟦こちら→こちら：00960_kochira⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧さんです.
- ⟦あいつ→あいつ：08267_aitsu⟧, ⟦こいつ→こいつ：08268_koitsu⟧ — that guy, this guy; rough, and affectionate only among close friends.
- ⟦{誰|だれ}→誰：00534_dare⟧ / ⟦どなた→どなた：02923_donata⟧ / ⟦どちら{様|さま}→どちら様：22795_dochirasama⟧ — who, in rising order of politeness; ⟦どちら{様|さま}→どちら様：22795_dochirasama⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ is how a receptionist asks your name.

## Tips for Learners

1. **Use names, not pronouns.** Name + ⟦さん→さん：09848_san⟧ is correct in almost every situation where English would say "you" or "he."
2. **Choose your "I" by the room.** ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧ is always safe; add ⟦{僕|ぼく}→僕：01729_boku⟧ or ⟦{俺|おれ}→俺：02185_ore⟧ (for men) and ⟦あたし→あたし：28132_atashi⟧ (for women) as your casual register develops.
3. **Learn both family sets.** ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧ to the outside, ⟦お{父|とう}さん→お父さん：02855_otousan⟧ to his face and for other people's fathers.
4. **Watch the inside/outside line.** Honorifics and titles come off your own people when you talk to outsiders, and go on other people's.
5. **Let people tell you.** ⟦{何|なん}→何〜：03100_nan⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}べば→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ (What should I call you?) is a normal and welcome question, and the answer settles the matter. See also [The Basic Keigo System](keigo.html) and [Greetings and Set Phrases](greetings.html).
